item.title: Bessent Misses Chance to Coordinate with a China-Wary Europe
item.description: There is an opportunity for a unified strategy with Europe. But the US is going it alone.

item.title: Tanker Carrying Qatari LNG Struck While Transiting Hormuz
item.description: A liquefied natural gas tanker carrying a shipment from Qatar was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to security intelligence firms and ship tracking data, threatening to further disrupt deliveries of the super-chilled fuel through the key waterway.

item.title: Indian Oil Buys Record Spot Market Crude on Mideast Supply Hit
item.description: Indian Oil Corp. bought a record share of its crude oil from the spot market in the April-June quarter after the US-Iran conflict upended supplies from the Middle East. The shift shows how geopolitical turmoil is forcing even the region’s biggest buyers to abandon long-established procurement strategies.

item.title: Europe’s Endless Heat Waves Imperil Once Reliable Power Sources
item.description: A series of blistering heat waves has weakened some of Europe’s most historically reliable sources of electricity, forcing the continent to lean more heavily on imported fossil fuels and variable renewable energy.

item.title: World Economy Latest: Central Banks Hold Rates Steady
item.description: Monetary policymakers from the US and the UK to Japan left interest rates unchanged this week as they assessed renewed inflation risks from higher energy costs and war in the Middle East.

item.title: How an Iron Ore Empire ‘Built on Trust’ Began to Sow Doubts
item.description: In a corporate presentation in December 2024, Radiant World boasted of its “diverse network” of suppliers and counterparties.

item.title: Germany’s Elusive Economic Revival Is Within Touching Distance
item.description: The long-awaited recovery of Europe’s largest economy is finally coming into view.

item.title: Bessent and the Fed Help Japan Reverse Months of Yen Losses
item.description: The US joined Japan in engineering one of the most notable rebounds in the yen since the currency began its years-long slide, a decline that’s stoked inflation in the Asian nation and rippled through global markets.

item.title: Modi Opposes Court Proceedings for Protesters, Urges Forgiveness
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he opposed punishment and court proceedings for the young protesters who marched in New Delhi and other Indian cities in recent weeks, saying “children make mistakes” and society should “forgive” them for using foul language.

item.title: India Push for Overseas Capital Draws Over $40 Billion, RBI Says
item.description: India’s push to attract overseas capital has brought in more than $40 billion since June, boosting the RBI’s foreign-currency buffers as policymakers seek to stabilize the rupee amid rising crude prices.

item.title: Macau Gaming Revenue Falls Again on Typhoon, World Cup
item.description: Macau’s gaming revenue fell 8.4% in July, declining for a second consecutive month as travel disruptions from Typhoon Noul and lingering distractions from the World Cup dented spending.

item.title: Orlopp to Hold UniCredit Talks on Commerzbank’s Fate, and Hers
item.description: Bettina Orlopp has about a week to prepare for a call that will set the stage for discussions about Commerzbank AG’s fate, and ultimately hers.

item.title: India’s Kerala Struggles to Care for Aging Population with Fertility Rate Low
item.description: India’s biggest student protests in years last week highlighted the growing frustrations of the country’s hundreds of millions of young people.

item.title: Lawmakers Unveil E15 Proposal Allowing Blending Exemptions
item.description: US lawmakers unveiled legislation that would expand sales of higher-ethanol gasoline and give exemptions from annual blending mandates for some small oil refineries that have received them in the past.

item.title: South Korea’s Exports Extend Momentum as Chip Boom Persists
item.description: South Korea’s exports extended their strong growth in July, reinforcing signs that artificial intelligence-driven demand continues to underpin the economy and strengthen the case for further monetary tightening.

item.title: Indian Firms Plan Fresh Price Hikes, Testing Inflation Outlook
item.description: India’s largest consumer companies are gearing to raise prices on products from toothpaste to tires and paint ahead of the festival season and for the second straight quarter, as the prolonged Middle East conflict drives up commodity costs and threatens to keep inflation elevated.

item.title: Google Rolls Back Earth AI Tool Over Concern About Fake Images
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google announced Friday that it will roll back its new AI image generation feature in Google Earth because some people were using it to create altered satellite imagery that appeared to violate the company’s policies.

item.title: New York City Spared Downgrade by Fitch and Moody’s, for Now
item.description: New York City avoided a debt downgrade Friday by two major credit-rating companies, though both warned the city must take steps to narrow projected deficits or risk a cut — despite the current boom on Wall Street.

item.title: New Zealand Housing Market Faces Biggest ‘Down Phase’ in Decades
item.description: New Zealand house prices fell to a three-year low in July, extending a slump that began in early 2022 and leaving the market in its weakest state in decades.

item.title: Hedge Funds Add Bullish Bets on Oil at Fastest Pace Since March
item.description: Hedge funds boosted bullish wagers on US oil at the fastest pace since March as supply disruptions from Iran to the Red and Black Seas are set to once again boost demand for American crude.

item.title: Extenet Bonds Miss Interest Amid Alleged Cash Control Violations
item.description: Bonds issued by Extenet Systems, a company that operates miniature cell towers, are in default after missing interest payments, and the firm also engaged in cash management violations, according to the bank responsible for collecting payments.

item.title: Biggest Wall Street Rotation Since 2020 Shows AI Crowding Risks
item.description: Wall Street staged a tentative recovery from one of the wildest weeks of the AI boom, belying a historic rotation beneath the surface that briefly exposed growing cracks in some of the grand assumptions underpinning global markets.

item.title: George Santos Must Pay $35,000 Over ‘Manipulative’ Kalshi Trade
item.description: Former Congressman George Santos agreed to pay more than $35,000 to settle allegations he manipulated a wager on prediction market platform Kalshi about whether he’d attend the 2026 State of the Union.

item.title: BlackRock’s ‘Widow Maker’ Treasury ETF Slides to 2004 Low
item.description: The rout in longer-dated US Treasuries has sent a popular BlackRock Inc. exchange-traded fund tumbling to its lowest level in over two decades, as concerns around sticky inflation continue battering fixed-income portfolios.

item.title: Trucking Stocks Fall on Legal Risk in Worst Month Since Tariffs
item.description: Trucking and logistics stocks are poised for their worst month in more than a year, weighed down by mounting concerns over a recent legal decision that can hurt industry brokers, alongside disappointing earnings.

item.title: Anthropic, OpenAI Cyber Failures Point to US Security Risks
item.description: Cybersecurity experts are faulting Anthropic PBC and OpenAI for sloppy safeguards after their models broke into outside organizations — breaches they warned represent looming threats to national security.

item.title: Colombia to Build Up Reserves as Peso Strengthens to 7-Year High
item.description: Colombia launched a program to accumulate as much $4 billion in international reserves, moving to weaken the nation’s currency from a seven-year high.

item.title: Big Tech Holds $2 Trillion of Spending Commitments for AI Boom
item.description: The four largest players in the data center race have committed nearly $2.4 trillion in spending over the coming years, pointing to massive ongoing investment in AI infrastructure.

item.title: Griffin’s Knack for Sniffing Out Trouble Set to Reward Citadel
item.description: It’s practically an adage on Wall Street by now: You know you’re in trouble when Ken Griffin calls.

item.title: Colombia Unexpectedly Holds Rates Despite Price Pressures
item.description: Colombia’s central bank unexpectedly held interest rates unchanged in the final monetary policy meeting under President Gustavo Petro’s administration despite mounting inflationary pressures.
